canonical_title: Philip K. Dick on Blade Runner
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A 1982 Starlog magazine feature carrying PKD's public reaction to the Blade Runner adaptation of Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, recorded shortly before his death and largely enthusiastic after early misgivings.
page_summary:
This Starlog feature preserves Philip K. Dick's public response to Blade Runner, Ridley Scott's adaptation of his 1968 novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? PKD died in March 1982, months before the film reached theaters, so his reaction survives from the pre-release period, when he had seen footage and special-effects work rather than the finished picture.

Having been wary of Hollywood and skeptical of an earlier draft of the screenplay, PKD came away impressed by what Scott's team had built, describing the future Los Angeles they created as matching the world he had imagined. The piece captures a novelist watching his interior vision rendered on screen at the very end of his life.

As the last substantial statement of PKD's on the adaptation that would carry his work to a mass audience, the interview is a primary document for the relationship between the novel, the film, and the author's own view of both.
